1| # Hook dispatch
2| 
3| How clud runs a repo's hooks itself, so they stop depending on where the agent
4| happens to be standing.
5| 
6| Design record: [#966](https://github.com/zackees/clud/issues/966) (spec),
7| [#967](https://github.com/zackees/clud/issues/967) (phased plan),
8| [#977](https://github.com/zackees/clud/issues/977) (settings compilation),
9| [#965](https://github.com/zackees/clud/issues/965) (the failure that started
10| it). Decisions: DD-047, DD-060, DD-061, DD-062, DD-063, DD-064.
11| 
12| ## The problem
13| 
14| A `cd` in a Bash tool call moves the **session** cwd, not just that command's.
15| Every later tool call inherits it. Hooks are conventionally written as
16| repo-relative script paths — `uv run python ci/hooks/check-on-stop.py` — so
17| once the cwd drifts, they resolve against the wrong directory and fail. When
18| the failing hook is a blocking one, nothing can run: the session wedges until a
19| human intervenes.
20| 
21| Three things follow from that, and they are what this subsystem exists to fix:
22| 
23| 1. Hooks must not depend on cwd.
24| 2. A nested repo's own hooks never load at all — the harness reads hooks only
25|    from the session root.
26| 3. The parent's hooks *do* keep firing inside a nested checkout, against files
27|    they know nothing about.
28| 
29| Upstream will not fix this: the cwd contract is documented as following the
30| agent, and the tracker's own reports disagree about whether cwd drifts or
31| silently resets (anthropics/claude-code#83636, #76708, #84685; the exact class
32| in #50960 and #42282 was closed NOT_PLANNED).
33| 
@ docs/architecture/hook-dispatch.md:85-129 [Repeated Stop-hook continuations] terms=1;path=2;heading=1;definition=1;distance=0
85| ## Repeated Stop-hook continuations
86| 
87| A `/goal` condition the sandbox cannot satisfy keeps the harness's Stop
88| evaluator re-prompting (#1597). That loop belongs to Claude Code: `/goal` is a
89| prompt-based Stop hook, and the docs give no precedence between it and another
90| Stop hook's output, so clud does not try to end the turn. The harness has its
91| own breakers: an "impossible" verdict, a no-progress stop, and a cap of 8
92| consecutive blocks.
93| 
94| clud only detects the loop. When `stop_hook_active` is true and
95| `last_assistant_message` is identical on 2 consecutive Stop events,
96| `stop_repeat.rs` prints one `systemMessage` that tells the user how to break
97| it. A different answer or a user-driven stop resets the count. `SessionEnd`
98| drops the per-session state file under `~/.clud/state/stop-repeat/`.
99| 
100| ## Declaring hooks
101| 
102| `<repo>/.clud/hooks.json`:
103| 
104| ```json
105| {
106|   "hooks": {
107|     "PreToolUse": [
108|       { "matcher": "Bash", "command": "uv run --frozen --no-sync python ci/hooks/check_cmd.py" }
109|     ],
110|     "Stop": [
111|       { "command": "uv run --frozen --no-sync python ci/hooks/check_on_stop.py", "timeout": 120 }
112|     ]
113|   }
114| }
115| ```
116| 
117| - `command` is a **shell command line**, the same shape both frontends accept.
118| - `matcher` is a regex over the tool name, anchored so `Edit` cannot catch
119|   `MultiEdit`. Absent or `"*"` matches everything. A pattern that will not
120|   compile falls back to exact equality — a declaration clud cannot understand
121|   should under-match, never over-match.
122| - `timeout` is seconds, defaulting to 60.
123| - Event names are free-form strings, so a declaration for an event clud has not
124|   learned to fire sits inert rather than failing the file.
125| 
126| Parsing is lenient in the same way `repo_clud_config` is: one malformed entry
127| is skipped with a warning rather than taking the file's other hooks down with
128| it.
129|

2| //!
3| //! Every `~/.clud`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` and managed-install path hangs off

8| //!
9| //! Precedence, the long-standing behavior of `clud_settings`:
10| //! - Windows: `USERPROFILE`, then `HOME`, then the OS profile folder.
11| //! - Elsewhere: `HOME`, then the OS lookup.

247| ### Grind skills require explicit invocation
248| 
249| The leaves and roles exist for the workflow, and for a person testing one by
250| hand; a model must never pick them up from an ordinary prompt.
251| 
252| - **All grind skills**, including `/grind`, have
253|   `disable-model-invocation: true` for Claude and Codex's
254|   `allow_implicit_invocation: false` policy. A person can still invoke them
255|   directly. The router reads `grind-intake` and `grind-cron` as files next to
256|   its own directory instead of invoking them.
257| - **The agent types** ignore that frontmatter, so they're still listed to the
258|   model. clud's PreToolUse hook refuses direct `Agent` calls to the internal
259|   execution roles. `grind-orchestrator` is the read-only router exception.
260|   The workflow's `agent()` spawns don't go
261|   through the `Agent` tool, so the workflow is unaffected.
262|   `CLUD_ALLOW_GRIND_AGENTS=1` lifts the block for testing a role by hand.
263| - **Each execution agent carries its procedure.** A hidden skill can't be loaded with
264|   the `Skill` tool or `skills:` preload, so `claude_files.rs` writes each
265|   agent file with its leaf skill's body appended. The skill remains the
266|   single source. The standalone orchestrator instructions live in its agent
267|   definition; it has no duplicate leaf skill.
